metadata.author: Christian Studer
metadata.description: A module to query the AssemblyLine API with a submission ID to get the submission report and parse it.
metadata.name: AssemblyLine Query
metadata.features:
The module requires the address of the AssemblyLine server you want to query as well as your credentials used for this instance. Credentials include the used-ID and an API key or the password associated to the user-ID.

The submission ID extracted from the submission link is then used to query AssemblyLine and get the full submission report. This report is parsed to extract file objects and the associated IPs, domains or URLs the files are connecting to.

Some more data may be parsed in the future.

The optional debug flag logs the full parsed MISP event, including indicators and classification tags, to the service logger. It is disabled by default. See https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/expansion/assemblyline_query.md.
metadata.input: Link of an AssemblyLine submission report.
metadata.output: MISP attributes & objects parsed from the AssemblyLine submission.

metadata.author: Christian Studer
metadata.name: CSV Import
metadata.description: Import MISP attributes from base64-encoded UTF-8 CSV contents.
metadata.features:
In order to parse data from a csv file, a header is required to let the module know which column is matching with known attribute fields / MISP types.

This header either comes from the csv file itself or is part of the configuration of the module and should be filled out in MISP plugin settings, each field separated by COMMAS. Fields that do not match with any type known in MISP or are not MISP attribute fields should be ignored in import, using a space or simply nothing between two separators (example: 'ip-src, , comment, ').

If the csv file already contains a header that does not start by a '#', you should tick the checkbox 'has_header' to avoid importing it and have potential issues. You can also redefine the header even if it is already contained in the file, by following the rules for headers explained earlier. One reason why you would redefine a header is for instance when you want to skip some fields, or some fields are not valid types.

For REST API requests, put the base64-encoded UTF-8 CSV contents in data; file is not a server-side path to read. See the [REST API guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/import_mod/csvimport.md).
metadata.input: Base64-encoded UTF-8 CSV contents in the JSON data field.
metadata.output: MISP Event attributes

header.message:
Define the header of the csv file, with types (included in MISP attribute types or attribute fields) separated by commas.
For fields that do not match these types or that you want to skip, please use space or simply nothing between commas.
For instance: ip-src,domain, ,timestamp

has_header.message: Tick this box ONLY if there is a header line, NOT COMMENTED, and all the fields of this header are respecting the recommendations above.

special_delimiter.message: IF THE DELIMITERS ARE NOT COMMAS, please specify which ones are used (for instance: ";", "|", "/", "	" for tabs, etc).

metadata.features:
This module can be used to import e-mail text as well as attachments and urls.
Configuration parameters are used to unzip attachments, guess zip attachment passwords, extract urls, remove common subject markers, and extract partial inline forwarded emails (extract_forwarded_emails, disabled by default): All switches default to False and accept JSON booleans, 0/1, and case-insensitive yes/no strings. Each block needs a sender address, a subject, and a recipient or date. At most 20 partial email objects are linked to the carrier with includes references. Plain text is preferred; HTML is used if no forwards are found in plain text. Reconstructed attributes have to_ids disabled; the original email is retained as evidence. Local or unparseable timestamps are preserved as text in the reconstructed headers. Existing extract_urls and remove_subject_markers settings also apply to forwards. URL objects are shared between the carrier and forwards that contain the same URL. Submitted EML/MSG bytes are preserved separately from converted EML and heuristic forwards. See the [usage guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/import_mod/email_import.md).

Some parameters can be given through the config dict. 'MISP_base_url_for_dynamic_link' is your MISP URL, to attach an hyperlink to your event on your MISP instance from the PDF. metadata.name: Extuno Lookup
metadata.features:
The module takes a store listing URL, or a `store:id` pair in a text attribute, and reports what Extuno knows about that artifact: whether it appears in the known-malicious catalog, with the threat type and the advisory it came from, and whether Extuno's own static and sandbox analysis reached a verdict on it.

It covers browser extensions (Chrome, Firefox, Edge), IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse), Discord client mods and the npm, PyPI, Packagist, Maven, WordPress and Open VSX registries. Browser and IDE extensions are the reason the module exists: they are not covered by OSV or any other public advisory database, so an extension id found on a workstation cannot be checked against one.

modules.name: GoAML Export
modules.description: This module is used to export MISP events containing transaction objects into GoAML format.

metadata.author: Christian Studer
metadata.description: This module is used to export MISP events containing transaction objects into GoAML format.
metadata.name: GoAML Export
metadata.features:
The module works as long as there is at least one transaction object in the Event.

Then in order to have a valid GoAML document, please follow these guidelines:
- For each transaction object, use either a bank-account, person, or legal-entity object to describe the origin of the transaction, and again one of them to describe the target of the transaction.
- Create an object reference for both origin and target objects of the transaction.
- A bank-account object needs a signatory, which is a person object, put as object reference of the bank-account.
- A person can have an address, which is a geolocation object, put as object reference of the person.

Supported relation types for object references that are recommended for each object are the folowing:
- transaction:
	- 'from', 'from_my_client': Origin of the transaction - at least one of them is required.
	- 'to', 'to_my_client': Target of the transaction - at least one of them is required.
	- 'address': Location of the transaction - optional.
- bank-account:
	- 'signatory': Signatory of a bank-account - the reference from bank-account to a signatory is required, but the relation-type is optional at the moment since this reference will always describe a signatory.
	- 'entity': Entity owning the bank account - optional.
- person:
	- 'address': Address of a person - optional.
metadata.input: MISP objects (transaction, bank-account, person, legal-entity, geolocation), with references, describing financial transactions and their origin and target.
metadata.output: GoAML format file, describing financial transactions, with their origin and target (bank accounts, persons or entities).

requirements: An IPGeolocation.io API key, or IPGeolocation.io MMDB databases stored on the misp-modules host
metadata.features:
The module takes an IP address attribute as input and answers from one of two sources:
- `api_key`: the [IPGeolocation.io API](https://ipgeolocation.io/documentation/ip-location-api.html). Free plans return geolocation and ASN. Paid plans also return the company, threat intelligence (`include=security`), the abuse contact (`include=abuse`) and the hostname; the `include` setting chooses these modules (default `security,abuse,hostname`, `none` for the base lookup only). If the plan does not allow them, the module falls back to the base lookup. Results are cached in memory for `cache_ttl` seconds (default 3600) to save credits on repeated lookups such as hover.
- `mmdb_paths`: comma-separated `.mmdb` files or directories of IPGeolocation.io databases: Location, Country, ISP, ASN, Company, Abuse Contact, Security (all versions), Residential Proxy and Hosting, or their combined editions. Names are returned in English. Lookups run locally and nothing is sent to IPGeolocation.io, which suits air-gapped instances and indicators that must not leave the organisation. Several databases are combined; for a field present in more than one, the first file in the list wins. Updated files are picked up automatically within a minute.

When `mmdb_paths` is set, the API is never called.

Tokens must match the selected API subscription. Lite does not include city, coordinates, postal code, hostname or timezone.

Privacy/anonymous flags, abuse contacts, company, carrier and other contextual fields returned by the selected plan are preserved in a JSON annotation referencing the input attribute. Explicit false flags are retained; absent fields do not imply a clean address. Hosted domains included in the response are added to the domain-ip object. No additional API endpoints are queried.

metadata.author: Tolga Sezer
metadata.description: Look up a SHA256 digest in the Malwagon sandbox and return the scans it already has for it.
metadata.name: Malwagon Lookup
requirements: A Malwagon API key with the read scope.
metadata.features:
The module takes a sha256 or filename|sha256 attribute and asks Malwagon which analyses it already holds for that digest. The lookup is free and answers immediately, so it is safe to use on hover: no sample leaves the MISP instance and no detonation quota is spent. Only the digest is sent.

Each analysis comes back as a sandbox-report object carrying the verdict, the score and a permalink to the report, referenced from a file object for the sample. The verdict is translated into MISP's own vocabulary - a misp:threat-level tag, plus ioc:artifact-state where the verdict is conclusive - rather than being passed through as a vendor string.

To detonate something Malwagon has never seen, use the Malwagon Submit module instead.
metadata.input: A sha256 or filename|sha256 attribute.
metadata.output: A file object for the sample and one sandbox-report object per Malwagon analysis, with the verdict expressed as MISP taxonomy tags.

modules.name: Malwagon Submit
modules.description: Detonate a sample or a URL in the Malwagon sandbox and return the analysis.

metadata.author: Tolga Sezer
metadata.description: Detonate a sample or a URL in the Malwagon sandbox and return the analysis.
metadata.name: Malwagon Submit
requirements: A Malwagon API key with the submit scope.
metadata.features:
The module takes an attachment, malware-sample or url attribute and detonates it in the Malwagon sandbox. A malware-sample arrives zip-encrypted with the password infected and is unpacked before submission.

A file is looked up by its SHA256 first. If Malwagon has already analysed that digest the existing analysis is returned, which is free, instant, and spends no detonation quota; set always_submit to force a fresh detonation instead. The module then polls the scan until it finishes or until poll_timeout seconds have passed, and returns what it has either way, so a long detonation gives back a permalink rather than an error.

This module submits the sample itself to a third party, so it is deliberately expansion-only and never runs on hover. Submission is blocked when the attribute carries a TLP tag more restrictive than max_tlp, and scans are created private unless private is set to false.

The sandbox image is chosen by the platform from the sample; on the free and community tiers the analysis virtual machine has no internet access at all, which is structural rather than a quota, so network-dependent samples will look inert there.
metadata.input: An attachment, malware-sample or url attribute.
metadata.output: A file object for the sample and a sandbox-report object for the Malwagon analysis, with the verdict expressed as MISP taxonomy tags.

metadata.author: Slava Olesik
metadata.description: Check a domain, hostname, URL or IP address against the NetAPI compromised feeds and get the domain's position in the NetAPI Top 1M.
metadata.name: NetAPI Lookup
metadata.features:
The module takes a domain, hostname, URL (by its host) or IP address attribute and queries the free compromised-check method of the NetAPI JSON API.

For a domain or hostname it says whether the value, or the registered domain a hostname belongs to, is in the NetAPI feed of hosts that public threat feeds report for malware or phishing: listed now (seen within the last 24 hours), listed in the past only, or never listed, with the first and last seen dates, the reporting feed and the registrar of the domain. A second free method, domain-rank, gives the position of the registered domain in the NetAPI Top 1M, a daily popularity ranking: a top-ranked domain in the feed is more likely a compromised legitimate site than infrastructure set up by the attacker.

For an IP address it checks the NetAPI compromised IP feed, the IPv4 addresses that attacked the sensors of NetAPI Nightwatch, NetAPI's own honeypot network: listed now (seen within the last 48 hours), listed in the past only, or never listed, with the first seen date, the time of the last attack and the type of attack. Private, loopback and reserved addresses are not sent.

The answer is a reputation object linked to the queried attribute: classification malicious when the value is listed now, suspicious when only its registered domain is, and unknown when it is listed in the past only or never (the feed holds no opinion on a value it does not list), with the first and last seen dates, a link to the NetAPI domain or IP lookup and the details (for a domain also the Top 1M rank) in its text.

No API key is required. An optional NetAPI API token only raises the request limits (30 requests a minute and 1,000 a day per IP address without one). Only the queried indicator leaves the MISP instance.
metadata.input: A domain, hostname, URL or IP address.
metadata.output: A reputation object with the feed listing and, for a domain, the Top 1M rank.

metadata.features: Parses captures offline with TShark, without capture privileges or network lookups. Extracts IPv4/IPv6 endpoints, DNS names and answers, HTTP URLs, hosts and user agents, and TLS SNI hostnames. Adds capture hashes and pcap-metadata, capture-scoped TCP/UDP network-connection objects, packet timestamps and observation intervals. Reconstructed content links to streams by exact payload hashes; identical content retains all observed sources. SMTP provenance uses a targeted second pass within the same timeout and combined metadata limit. See the [usage guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/import_mod/pcap_import.md).

requirements: ptrclassify and dnspython Python libraries; DNS access for IP lookups
metadata.features:
IPv4 and IPv6 attributes are reverse-resolved and every distinct PTR hostname is classified locally using ptrclassify's built-in rules, retaining the queried address to detect IP-encoded naming. Hostname and domain attributes are classified directly, without DNS or an API key. Matching ptrclassify taxonomy tags are added to the queried attribute, retaining its UUID and existing tags, and to PTR answers in a `dns-record` object. One `ptrclassify` object per hostname holds the classification labels, confidence, evidence, rule IDs and potential location hints. Repeated classification fields share the machine tag as their attribute comment; location fields share a rule-ID/code comment. Classification objects reference the queried attribute and, for IP lookups, the DNS object. No match returns an object with `matched=0` without adding tags. Configure `nameserver` to use a specific DNS server; otherwise the system resolver is used. DNS lookups have a five-second lifetime.

Classification is heuristic: PTR names are operator-controlled, and inferred locations are hints, not verified geolocation. Hover displays the enrichment; importing the expansion applies the returned tags in MISP. Enable the ptrclassify taxonomy in MISP to manage these tags, and install the ptrclassify MISP object template. The module bundles the template so it also works with PyMISP versions that do not yet include it.

Start misp-modules with --debug to log the command, live CLI output, elapsed time and report summary; this also enables Sherlock's --verbose output. --debug-extended HTTP tracing runs in the server process and cannot trace Sherlock's separate process. For troubleshooting, first limit sites to GitHub. Results can contain false positives and should be reviewed.

metadata.author: Atif Nazir

metadata.name: SoChain
metadata.features:
Query the SoChain API v3 for a btc attribute or a coin-address object. A btc attribute is looked up on Bitcoin. A coin-address object is looked up on the network named by its symbol (BTC, LTC, DOGE or ZEC); without a symbol, the network is the first of Bitcoin, Litecoin, Dogecoin and Zcash on which SoChain says the address is valid.

The result is a coin-address object with the balance, total received and sent, the number of transactions and the first and last activity, referencing the input. Recent counterparties are returned as coin-address objects linked with `paid` references (5 on hover, 50 when the magnifying glass is clicked), whose comments give the amount, transaction and block. When look-alike addresses sent the address dust to poison its history, each one is returned as a coin-address object that `impersonates` the address it copies.

No API key is needed for up to 2,500 lookups a day per IP. With a key from https://sochain.com/dashboard, lookups count against that account's plan.
metadata.input: A btc attribute, or a coin-address object with a BTC, LTC, DOGE or ZEC address.

metadata.features:
Query vulnerability identifiers or CPEs. Import linked advisories, comments, bundles, sightings, storage metadata, EPSS scores and known-exploited assertions as related MISP content. Enable with_timeline to include dated milestones as an annotation.
api_url defaults to https://vulnerability.circl.lu (instance root, without /api). timeout defaults to 30 seconds per request (maximum 120). max_related defaults to 50 (0-100): it bounds alias lookup attempts, CPE results and each enrichment section. with_linked, with_comments, with_bundles, with_sightings, with_meta, with_epss and with_kev default to true; with_timeline defaults to false. Original advisory JSON is retained as a base64 payload; community, EPSS and KEV records retain JSON attachments. Unavailable optional data does not discard the advisory. The companion vulnerability-sighting, epss-score and known-exploited-vulnerability templates are bundled for compatibility with existing PyMISP releases.

For a domain it queries the WHOIS, DNS and Domain Reputation APIs; for an IP address it queries the IP WHOIS, Geolocation and IP Security APIs. All lookups for a given attribute are executed in parallel.
metadata.name: WhoisFreaks Lookup
requirements: An access to the Whoisfreaks API_KEY
metadata.features:
The module takes a domain or an IP address as input.

For a domain it queries the Whoisfreaks WHOIS (v1.0), DNS (v2.0) and Domain Reputation APIs in parallel. For an IP address it queries the IP WHOIS, Geolocation and IP Security APIs in parallel.

The results are mapped to MISP attributes, objects (geolocation, asn, reputation and security) and tags.
metadata.input: A domain or an IP address (ip-src, ip-dst or ip).
metadata.output: MISP attributes, objects and tags resulting from the WhoisFreaks WHOIS, DNS, Domain Reputation, IP WHOIS, Geolocation and IP Security APIs.

metadata.description: Look up Wikidata labels and aliases and return related annotation objects.
metadata.name: Wikidata Lookup
metadata.features: Looks up exact labels and aliases in Wikidata without an API key. Returns bounded candidate matches with labels, descriptions and Wikidata links as annotation objects related to the source text attribute. Generated attributes have to_ids=false. language defaults to en; max_results defaults to 5 (1-25); timeout defaults to 15 seconds (1-60). Blank settings use defaults. Labels and descriptions fall back to English when unavailable in the requested language. No matches returns an empty Object list. Legacy top-level text requests are accepted, but all responses use misp_standard.
metadata.input: A text attribute containing type, value and UUID; legacy top-level text is also accepted.
metadata.output: Annotation objects with Wikidata links, labels and descriptions, in MISP standard format.

metadata.author: XposedOrNot
metadata.description: Query the XposedOrNot API to check whether an email address appears in known data breaches.
metadata.name: XposedOrNot Lookup
metadata.features: The module takes an email address as input and queries the XposedOrNot API to determine whether the address appears in known data breaches. Each exposure is returned as a breach object holding the breach name, date, number of exposed records, affected domain, exposed data classes and password storage risk. Without any configuration the free keyless API is used (rate limits apply: 2 requests/second, 25/hour per IP); an optional commercial api_key switches to the higher-limit Plus API. The queried email address is sent over TLS to xposedornot.com; nothing else leaves the MISP instance.
metadata.input: An email address.
metadata.output: One breach object per data breach the email address appears in.

metadata.author: Christophe Vandeplas
metadata.description: Export stored YARA collections and optionally generate literal IOC content searches.
metadata.name: YARA Rule Export
metadata.features: Produces a ZIP of unchanged stored YARA collections in separate namespaces, with a provenance and exclusion manifest. The default both mode exports yara attributes regardless of to_ids and generates literal, case-sensitive UTF-8 byte searches from supported IDS-marked attributes. Select rules or indicators to export only stored collections or generated IOC searches, respectively. A filename or domain matches bytes in scanned content, not a file's name or DNS activity. Deleted data is excluded. Collections and the complete output are compiled with filesystem includes disabled. See the [usage guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/export_mod/yara_export.md).
metadata.input: MISP events and object attributes in standard, bare or legacy export format.
metadata.output: Base64-encoded ZIP containing rules/*.yara and manifest.json; load using the manifest namespaces.

metadata.author: MISP Project
metadata.name: Zeek Observations Import
metadata.description: Import selected Zeek records with timestamps, connection/Community IDs and capture provenance.
metadata.features: Accepts native JSON/JSONL and typed Zeek ASCII logs, including escaped/unset fields. Preserves raw records, stream/sensor context, exact timestamps, UIDs, Community IDs, notices/signatures and capture references. Reuses network-connection and pcap-metadata with a bundled network-observation template. UID selection omits the full source attachment when records are excluded. All observations remain unreviewed and non-IDS. No Zeek execution, capture access or network calls. See the [usage guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-modules/blob/main/documentation/import_mod/zeek_import.md).
metadata.input: Base64-encoded UTF-8 Zeek JSON/JSONL or ASCII log; JSON requires explicit stream context.
metadata.output: Source file, network-observation, network-connection and optional pcap-metadata objects.

modules.name: ZoomEye
modules.description: Search ZoomEye API v2 for IP addresses, domains, hostnames and SHA-1 certificate fingerprints.

metadata.author: Alexandre Dulaunoy
metadata.name: ZoomEye
metadata.description: Search ZoomEye API v2 for IP addresses, domains, hostnames and SHA-1 certificate fingerprints.
metadata.features: Requires `api_key`. Builds an escaped, Base64-encoded search query for API v2 and requests one page of up to `max_results` assets (default 20, maximum 100). Uses the v4/v6 dataset for IPs, web for domains, and all datasets for hostnames and certificate fingerprints. Leading/trailing API key whitespace is removed. A result-limit notice is included when total exceeds the returned records; additional pages are not fetched automatically. Returns referenced ip-port objects with service/banner context, and an annotation retaining result counts and observed metadata. Certificate searches identify assets using an observed certificate, not a malicious verdict. All enrichment has to_ids disabled.
metadata.input: ip-src, ip-dst, domain, hostname, x509-fingerprint-sha1 MISP attribute.
metadata.output: Referenced ip-port objects and an annotation with result count and search coverage.
